items.title: Remove Extraneous Imports in Pages
items.body:
This plugin removes unused imports from a page, regardless of whether or not they're pure.

Only imports that appear to be a side effect are retained:
```js
import 'im-probably-a-side-effect';
```

Since this behavior could be "breaking", it's only enabled when someone is using the new `getStaticProps` lifecycle method.
We'll also turn this on for the (not-yet-implemented) `getServerProps`.

---

tl;dr this PR allows you to import server-only modules like `fs` for your `getStaticProps` method, and not need to edit webpack to exclude it. **Less code to the frontend!**

items.title: Refactor Webpack Configuration
items.body:
This pull request takes the first step in refactoring some of our webpack configuration.

The objective is to make it more composable, and isolate certain sections of behavior for ease of reading.

This introduces the concept of "Configuration Blocks" and a "Configuration Builder".

The "Configuration Blocks" are meant to fully encapsulate certain behaviors, e.g. CSS or Experiments.

The "Configuration Builder" applies these blocks in the correct order -- it accepts and emits a configuration object the same way our `next.config.js` Webpack customization does.

Let's see if tests pass. 😄

items.title: [with-react-intl] Fix message extraction script on consecutive builds

labels.name: examples
labels.description: Issue was opened via the examples template.

items.body:
I wasn't aware, but it seems like Next doesn't do a fresh build every time `next build` is run -- unchanged files that have already passed through Babel are skipped on subsequent runs. Unfortunately, that breaks message extraction (via [babel-plugin-react-intl](https://github.com/formatjs/formatjs/tree/master/packages/babel-plugin-react-intl)) in this example: on subsequent runs it'll fail to extract messages in unchanged files, leaving the list of strings shorter than it should be (or just completely empty)!

This PR fixes that case by simply removing the `.next` directory before building. It also relaxes the requirement in the helper script forbidding duplicate message IDs -- they're allowed if their corresponding messages are identical, which is the same rule enforced by babel-plugin-react-intl on a per-file basis.

Main problem is that the test previously checked for the rendered HTML **not** to contain a certain string, but the string doesn't really make sense (I think it's a typo in #8960) and would never appear in the HTML anyway: `<meta name="width=device-width"/>`

My proposal for this test is, instead of checking for all kinds of strings that are not supposed to be in the rendered HTML, I think it's better to count and check the number of occurrences.

I will shortly submit another test more related to my actual issue, which this test does not cover.

items.title: Ensure params in query are updated for custom-routes
items.body:
This matches the behavior in `@now/routing-utils` which will replace params in the query e.g. `?name=:something` and it also makes sure we don't drop previous query values for rewrites since that is not the case in Now.

For redirects we only replace params in the query and don't pass them through for example, for the redirect `{ source: '/:name', destination: '/another?first=:name` and we request `/hello?a=b` we don't pass through the `a=b` query value only `first=hello`. This should also mirror the behavior in Now

There was a weird issue I encountered where the compiled `renderer` output needs to be located under `renderer/out`. If I copied it just to `renderer`, it would throw a 404 error. That's why I changed `'../renderer/index.html'` to `'../renderer/out/index.html'`

Also made a few smaller changes:
- Updated `electron-next` types

- Updated `dist` script to use `electron-builder` instead of `electron-builder --dir`. The former is what actually creates an installer a user can run in production while the latter is an unpacked directory useful for development

items.title: Proposing a new example "with-typescript-graphql"

labels.name: examples
labels.description: Issue was opened via the examples template.

items.body:
# Why There are many good examples already but I'd like to propose a new one to achieve the thought of [Apollo Data Graph](https://www.apollographql.com/#architecture) and writing purely type-protected code in TypeScript by [GraphQL Code Generator](https://graphql-code-generator.com/) (graphql-codegen). ## Apollo Data Graph as BFF Owning a GraphQL server endpoint in charge of front-end devs widens technical options. With resolvers of Apollo Server, it conciliates any kind of external resources not only databases but REST APIs, Elasticsearch/other middlewares and even other GraphQL APIs to beautifully render view. Which is, so-called [BFF](https://developer.ibm.com/patterns/create-backend-for-frontend-application-architecture/). Next.js has a great fit for the role of BFF. Here I respectfully used the [Apollo Server and Client Example](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/api-routes-apollo-server-and-client#readme) as the code base, which perfectly achieved SSR and providing an easy way to integrate Apollo Client with [`withApollo`](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/examples/api-routes-apollo-server-and-client/apollo/client.js) HOC utility. Users will easily know how to expand GraphQL types/resolvers with the initial structure. ## TypeScript, graphql-codegen and graphql-let graphql-codegen is a great tool to apply types of GraphQL schema to component development by generating additional `.tsx`s. Only, it has to be executed to follow the latest schema and force users to manage generated `.tsx` files and then import them respectively. [graphql-let](https://github.com/piglovesyou/graphql-let#readme) that I've recently published connects the GraphQL documents and the codegen results as close as below, as it keeps giving benefits of TypeScript types, where users might almost forget code generation. ```typescript jsx import { useNewsQuery } from './news.graphql' const News: React.FC<{}> = (props) => { // Typed already️⚡️ const { data: { news } } = useNewsQuery() if (news)
{news.map(...)}
} ``` ## Accelerate the type-protected GraphQL development Once I got used to the typed-BFF development style, where I declare all the types of external resources in GraphQL schema and write components using the statically and dynamically type-assured data as just I declared, I can't go back. Thankfully to the Node ecosystem, it's not too hard to set up that environment from scratch, but I thought it's a good idea for us to have a clean template to make it work out of the box in Next.js examples. I'll draw a quick feature comparison table of the existing examples. | Name | GraphQL Client | GraphQL Server | TypeScript | Typed data (Codegen) | | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | [with-apollo](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-apollo) | ✔︎ | | | | | [with-apollo-and-redux](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-apollo-and-redux) | ✔︎ | | | | | [with-apollo-and-redux-saga](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-apollo-and-redux-saga) | ✔︎ | | | | | [api-routes-graphql](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/api-routes-graphql) | | ✔︎ | | | | [api-routes-apollo-server-and-client](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/api-routes-apollo-server-and-client) | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | | | | [with-typescript](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-typescript) | | | ✔︎ | | | [with-typescript-graphql](https://github.com/piglovesyou/next.js/tree/example/with-typescript-graphql/examples/with-typescript-graphql) | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ | ✔︎ |

items.title: Optimize Prefetching
items.body:
This pull request optimizes our page loader's prefetching by changing the following:

- Uses `prefetch` instead of `preload` when available (so resource loads as low-priority). This lessens CPU load during hydration. 
    * `preload` is still required for macOS (Safari) and iOS (iOS Safari).
    * https://caniuse.com/#feat=link-rel-prefetch (standard, new default)
    * https://caniuse.com/#feat=link-rel-preload (proposal, old default)
- A smaller data saver detection snippet was copied from [`quicklink`](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/quicklink)
- Fallback-`<script>` preloading loading was removed as it was for backwards compat, which is now covered by wider-supported `prefetch`
- Other code golfing techniques to reduce footprint

Contrary to an assumption we were operating on (IIRC), `preload` does not preparse the script. In fact, `prefetch` should actually have better caching characteristics (forces storage in disk cache instead of in-memory, meaning less data transferred on n+1 visit).

Only `<link rel="modulepreload">` (Chrome + ESModules only) parses a script prior to execution.

items.title: Add selenium-webdriver and testing cross-browser in PRs
items.body:
This investigates replacing `wd` with `selenium-webdriver` using a shim to mock the syntax of `wd` to allow us to not have to rewrite all of our browser interactions. The goal of this PR is to allow testing in `safari`, `firefox`, `ie11`, and `chrome` without relying on BrowserStack. 

Not relying on BrowserStack to test in these browsers allows us to test in each PR and not having to wait until merging to `canary` to see if something is breaking in a certain browser. It also allows us to test locally without eating up our limit in BrowserStack. 

Using the `selenium-webdriver` package also allows us to pass a `CHROME_BIN` path in the environment and use it instead of the default one.

While testing locally it appears to be working in `firefox`, `ie11`, `chrome`, and `safari` < 13 `safaridriver` is broken on version 13 see [here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/58289949) for more info) and seems to be why BrowserStack doesn't even offer this version yet

**Update:** Looks like we may still need to rely on BrowserStack for `safari` testing on merge since CircleCi doesn't appear to be able to enable `allow remote automation` and `safaridriver`

items.title: Fix _app global css import order
items.body:
Hello,

First of all, thanks for all the work you all have put into nextjs, I and my team really appreciate it.

We have recently configured our project to import css files directly from their respective react components and also got css splitting working.

The only problem we have is when importing global/third-party css. We import them in our custom _app file, but the split page css keeps getting added to page head before our global/third-party css. This causes our third-party customizations to be overwritten by their original styles.

After debugging and examining nextjs code I have found two points where, it seems, "root" components (like _document and _app) are imported after the page component and that's causing their chunks to be added after the page chunks, causing the problems I described above.

As custom _app and _document are supposed to act as root components for our nextjs apps, nextjs users expect that those components and their dependencies to be imported first. I say that based on
https://github.com/zeit/next-plugins/issues/399
https://spectrum.chat/next-js/general/control-the-placement-of-styles-chunk-css-in-nextjs7~0d91eec7-6a38-4943-98f6-0bb3a71d50f6
and a few other cases I found while looking for a solution for this.

We are currently using a custom extended HEAD component that reorder our css files attaching first our global styles as a workaround (not pretty at all xD).

The changes in this PR fix the issue.
